anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After: both outputs already fold AC2/AC3/AC5 into a single 'Deferred/deviates per spec' line, surface only the AC4 latency gap as the one decision item (N=1 in both the status header and the operator view), say nothing about re-auditing the drift line, and, when recommending none, name the missing prerequisites (maxFixRounds 0, no tracker convention) while carrying G1 open with no auto-applied fix. So the 'fails -> holds' expectations for f1–f3 are not borne out by this pair; Before was already settling elsewhere rows correctly, meaning the Change is either not exercised by this case or was already satisfied. Two incidental drifts in After worth watching: 'round history' changed from 'R0 PARTIAL (recommended: accept)' to 'none', which drops the reviewer's accept token from the card body (it survives only in the rationale), and 'whole-diff minors' changed from 'none' to 'not recorded' with no source for that wording in the reviewer report. To keep f6 robust, keep the reviewer's recommended token visible in round history (e.g. 'R0 PARTIAL (reviewer recommended: accept); no fix round run (maxFixRounds 0)') and keep 'whole-diff minors: none' when the report lists none.

The expected-to-move facts already held in Before for this case, so the Change is delivered without regression. Two After-only differences are worth watching: the handoff block no longer repeats the Deferred/deviates line (fine for f1, but if a consumer expects it in the handoff, keep one copy there), and After injects a provisional 'freshness check cannot be performed without tools' preamble plus a 'Step 4 cannot render yet' justification that references freshness rather than only the undisposed decision — that extra gating reason is not in the spec or reviewer report and could be read as a second blocker. Keep the elsewhere-rows wording as is; drop the freshness caveat or tie Step 4's withholding solely to the unresolved decision, as Before did.
